command_or_fixture: Scratch probe on macOS: hdiutil-attached 4 MiB HFS+ image mounted at <tmp>/repo/.wavefoundry/work/mntky holding precious.txt and d/z; opened via wave_work._parent and os.open(key, _FLAGS, dir_fd=parent); ran the real _empty_directory with a verify closure of _anchor + _entry (the planned closure minus the owner re-read). counterexample_or_failure_condition: Apply on .wavefoundry/work/<key> where <key> is a mount point (RAM disk, disk image, devcontainer or WSL2 bind mount from another filesystem) deletes every file on that volume.

artifact_or_test_id: wave_work._read_owner (O_NONBLOCK, S_ISREG, st_nlink, 4096 bound); scratch probe p.py (deleted)
command_or_fixture: Scratch probe: os.mkfifo(<work>/fffff/.owner.json); os.open(path, O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW) under a 2 s SIGALRM; then the same open with O_NONBLOCK.
counterexample_or_failure_condition: A FIFO named .owner.json makes a plain no-follow open block forever, so apply hangs while holding project_state_publication_lock and stalls every lifecycle writer; a multi-GB .owner.json is hashed once per entry deleted; a directory or symlink named .owner.json has no defined fingerprint.
expected: A bounded, non-blocking read with a defined result for non-regular or oversized owner files.
known_bad_detection_method: FIFO owner fixture blocked the naive open; refuted plan claim.
limitations: Did not measure hashing cost of a large file. Preview also reads the fingerprint on native Windows, not executed there.
observed: The plain open BLOCKED until the 2 s alarm; with O_NONBLOCK it opened and fstat showed S_ISFIFO.
proposition: 23q0s Requirements 4 and 5 define the owner fingerprint as 'the SHA-256 of the raw .owner.json bytes or absent' and re-read it before every unlink and rmdir, but state no read rules. Because the closure deliberately skips _read_owner, it also loses _read_owner's O_NONBLOCK open, fstat regular-file check, st_nlink check and 4096-byte bound. The owner file in an unowned folder is untrusted.
public_path: Refuted plan claim: 23q0s Requirement 4 fingerprint definition, exercised against the os.open primitive the fingerprint read must use (the tool itself is unimplemented).
safety_and_authorization: Scratch directory only.

disposition_rationale: Smallest plan change: Requirement 4 defines the fingerprint as read with O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, fstat-checked regular file, at most 4096 bytes; any other kind or size yields a fixed marker in the token and apply refuses it as unsafe_owner_entry; add an AC-3 case: FIFO and oversized .owner.json refuse promptly with the tree unchanged.

command_or_fixture: Scratch probe: replaced <tmp>/repo/.wavefoundry/work with a symlink to an outside directory; wave_work._parent refused (NotADirectoryError, errno 20) but os.scandir on the work-root path listed the outside directory's entries.

counterexample_or_failure_condition: The implementer writes a second key-to-wave classifier inside upgrade_wavefoundry.py (or imports server_impl there). The upgrade report then classifies differently from close and audit, for example under a renamed record-root profile or an archive root, and no criterion detects it.
expected: One classification helper importable without the MCP server (built on record_paths.discover_wave_dirs, record_paths.discover_archive_dirs, vocabulary_profile and the record status parse), called by close, audit, the upgrade report and wf_cleanup_work; or the upgrade leftovers produced only in-process by wf_upgrade_response with the CLI-print path stated as out of scope.
known_bad_detection_method: Refuted plan claim by locating the helper definitions and the upgrade process imports.

The requirement therefore cannot be met for one of its three callers without either importing the 26k-line MCP server module into the upgrade process or writing a second classifier, which defeats the one-inventory design and AC-3.5's vocabulary-profile guarantee (AC-3.5 tests the inventory, not the upgrade caller).
